claims.text: The random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution has substantial lattice distortion.
HfNbTaTiZr has a thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Lattice distortion and defects suppress electron and phonon propagation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic size mismatch and chemical disorder are specifically responsible for strong phonon scattering in random HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr forms specific HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr clusters develop local B2-like chemical order.
Controlled annealing or Monte Carlo-guided phase selection can induce the proposed ordered state.
Specific pair interactions can promote chemical ordering and phase formation in compositionally complex alloys.
The ordered binary clusters undergo a percolative transition and form continuous pathways.
B2-like ordering locally regularizes the HfNbTaTiZr lattice and reduces atomic root-mean-square displacements.
Chemical short-range order can flatten a local energy landscape.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS of HfNbTaTiZr to higher frequencies because of stiffer bonds.
The higher-frequency DOS is accompanied by increased phonon group velocities.
Percolating ordered clusters create low-resistance heat-transport pathways whose benefit exceeds scattering at cluster boundaries.
The ordered HfNbTaTiZr state will have higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random state.
The conductivity increase occurs only after the ordered clusters exceed a connectivity or percolation threshold.
The stability of an ordered phase is bounded by an order-disorder transition temperature determined by site occupancy and interaction energies.
Decomposition into brittle Laves-type intermetallics or loss of order will lower conductivity through additional scattering or phase-boundary resistance.
Higher-frequency DOS peaks and lower atomic displacement parameters in the ordered sample would accompany the proposed conductivity increase.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator invokes a flattened local potential-energy landscape, while the mechanism invokes stiffer bonds and higher-frequency modes. These can coexist only if 'flattening' means reduced spatial or chemical-energy fluctuations rather than reduced local potential curvature; that distinction is not stated.
